questions.text: Your older sibling is secretly dating someone and hiding their phone. How do you find out the truth?

options.A: Follow them casually to the tuition center, keeping a safe distance, to see exactly who they meet after class.
options.B: Figure out their new phone passcode by analyzing their thumb movements and the smudge marks on the screen.
options.C: Sneak a peek at their WhatsApp notifications using a strategically placed mirror or by pretending to search for something near their phone.
options.D: Blackmail their best friend with an embarrassing secret to get them to confess the exact details to you.

questions.text: You got a terrible score in your Math unit test. How do you handle the situation with your strict parents?

options.A: Confidently act completely normal, intercept the report card from the teacher, and physically hide it deep in your bag.
options.B: Carefully forge your parent's signature by analyzing the exact pressure points, loops, and curves of their real signature.
options.C: Use your phone to secretly record audio of your parents talking to gauge their mood before deciding when to break the news.
options.D: Coordinate with your siblings to create a master plan, telling them exactly what to say to distract mom if she asks about the test.

questions.text: When you watch Bollywood spy movies like Pathaan, Ek Tha Tiger, or Raazi, which character do you relate to the most?

options.A: The rugged spy who travels under a fake identity, fights the villains hand-to-hand, and jumps across rooftops.
options.B: The smart tech-genius in the van typing furiously on multiple screens, unlocking vault doors and servers in seconds.
options.C: The person who creates the high-tech explosive chewing gum, camera pens, and invisible fingerprint gloves.
options.D: The strict boss in the Delhi headquarters who looks at the big screen and commands, 'Bring him back, the mission is compromised.'

questions.text: The colony aunties are gossiping about a huge scandal in the society park. How do you get the 'tea'?

options.A: Casually walk past them with your cycle, pretending to fix the chain while actually listening to every word.
options.B: Piece together the half-sentences you heard and cross-reference them with society WhatsApp group messages to find the truth.
options.C: Leave your phone recording voice notes hidden under a nearby park bench and retrieve it after they leave.
options.D: Send your younger sibling with a plate of pakoras to offer them, instructing them to listen carefully and report back to you.

questions.text: You're playing an intense game of Chuppan Chupai (hide-and-seek) during a power cut. What is your strategy?

options.A: Keep moving silently from room to room, using the shadows to actively dodge the seeker in the dark.
options.B: Memorize the layout of the furniture and count the seeker's footsteps to calculate exactly which room they are in.
options.C: Find the most visually impossible hiding spot, blending in perfectly behind the heavy drawing-room curtains without moving a muscle.
options.D: Tell the other hiders exactly where to hide to confuse the seeker, while you take the ultimate, safest spot for yourself.

questions.text: Your friends are planning a surprise birthday for you, but you already suspect it. What do you do?

options.A: Play along flawlessly, acting completely shocked and surprised when you walk into the room so they don't feel bad.
options.B: Analyze their changing schedules and the sudden silence when you enter the classroom to deduce the exact date and time.
options.C: Casually glance at their phone notifications when it lights up on the desk to see the name of the secret WhatsApp group.
options.D: Secretly manipulate the situation so they end up planning the party at your favorite cafe instead of the boring school canteen.

questions.text: Someone ate the last piece of cake from the fridge, and everyone in the family is denying it. How do you solve this mystery?

options.A: Interrogate everyone face-to-face, staring into their eyes and looking for sweat, hesitation, or a guilty expression.
options.B: Check the dustbin for the exact timeline of thrown wrappers and match it logically with who was awake at what time.
options.C: Check the kitchen floor for accidental crumbs or inspect the fridge handle for sticky chocolate fingerprints using a flashlight.
options.D: Gather everyone in the living room and declare like a judge that nobody leaves until the true culprit confesses.

questions.text: Your mom lost her expensive gold ring in the house and is panicking. How do you help her find it?

options.A: Get on your hands and knees, searching under beds, behind sofas, and physically turning the house upside down.
options.B: Retrace her exact steps from the morning, logically eliminating the rooms she definitely didn't enter.
options.C: Use your phone's flashlight at a low angle across the floor tiles to catch the shiny glint of the gold.
options.D: Assign one room to each family member and coordinate the search like a massive, organized rescue operation.

questions.text: It's the school Annual Day and the electricity suddenly goes out right before the main play. What is your reaction?

options.A: Run to the backstage area physically to calm the actors down and make sure nobody panics in the dark.
options.B: Quickly figure out if it's a tripped fuse or a neighborhood power cut by checking the streetlights outside the window.
options.C: Immediately turn on your phone's flashlight and use it as a makeshift spotlight so the play can continue.
options.D: Take charge, order the volunteers to secure the doors, and send someone specifically to find the electrician.

questions.text: If you actually got recruited by RAW (Research and Analysis Wing) or IB (Intelligence Bureau), what would be your dream job?

options.A: Living in a foreign country under a fake name, speaking a new language, and gathering top-secret intel in person.
options.B: Sitting in a secure, dark room cracking an impossible enemy communication code that saves millions of lives.
options.C: Getting access to a secret government lab full of micro-drones, laser microphones, and advanced tracking devices.
options.D: Being the mastermind in Delhi who plans the entire global operation, moves the agents like chess pieces, and outsmarts the enemy.

Undercover_Agent.title: The Phantom (Undercover Field Agent)
Undercover_Agent.primary_match_text: You are action-oriented, fearless, and a phenomenal actor! You love the thrill of being in the center of the action and rely on your street smarts. In an intelligence agency, you would be the undercover spy operating in disguise, living in foreign territories, and extracting dangerous secrets firsthand.
Undercover_Agent.day_in_the_life: You wake up in a different country under a completely fake identity. You meet informants in busy cafes, tail suspects through narrow streets, and use your charm to extract top-secret information without blowing your cover.
Undercover_Agent.alternative_match_text: If not a spy, you would make an incredible Investigative Journalist, Private Detective, or a Commando in the Special Forces (Para SF).
Undercover_Agent.roadmap: Take any stream in 11th/12th. Pursue a BA or BSc. Learning a foreign language (like Mandarin, Arabic, or Pashto) from JNU or EFLU gives you a massive advantage. Entry into IB/RAW often requires clearing the UPSC Civil Services (IPS route) or SSC CGL for the Intelligence Bureau.

Cryptanalyst.title: The Codebreaker (Cryptanalyst / Interceptor)
Cryptanalyst.primary_match_text: You are a highly analytical genius who spots patterns that others miss. You don't need to be on the battlefield to win the war; you use your brain to dismantle the enemy. As a Cryptanalyst, you would intercept enemy calls, break complex passwords, and decode hidden messages.
Cryptanalyst.day_in_the_life: You sit in a highly secure, high-tech facility in India. You wear headphones, listening to intercepted radio frequencies from across the border. You use complex mathematics to break enemy encryption codes, finding the hidden date and time of an impending attack.
Cryptanalyst.alternative_match_text: If not in Intelligence, you would thrive as a Cybersecurity Expert, Ethical Hacker, or Data Scientist.
Cryptanalyst.roadmap: Take PCM (Physics, Chemistry, Math) in 11th/12th. Pursue a B.Tech in Computer Science, Mathematics, or Statistics. Get certifications in Ethical Hacking and Cryptography. Direct recruitment happens for technical wings of IB and NTRO (National Technical Research Organisation) via GATE or specific defense exams.

Surveillance_Expert.title: The Tech Observer (Surveillance & Gadget Expert)
Surveillance_Expert.primary_match_text: You are resourceful, creative, and love high-tech gadgets! You believe the best way to defeat an enemy is to see everything they do without them knowing. As a Surveillance Expert, you would develop and deploy spy tech, drones, and hidden cameras.
Surveillance_Expert.day_in_the_life: You are either in a lab building a camera that fits inside a button, or out in the field flying a silent micro-drone over an enemy hideout. You provide the crucial visual intel that helps the field agents survive.
Surveillance_Expert.alternative_match_text: If not in Intelligence, you would be an amazing Drone Pilot, Forensic Expert, or Robotics Engineer.
Surveillance_Expert.roadmap: Take PCM in 11th/12th. Pursue a B.Tech in Electronics, Robotics, or a BSc in Forensic Science. Specialize in surveillance technologies or signals intelligence. You can join DRDO as a scientist or enter NTRO to handle India's premier surveillance satellites and tech.

Mission_Handler.title: The Mastermind (Mission Handler / Intel Director)
Mission_Handler.primary_match_text: You are a strategic leader who sees the big picture. You are calm under pressure and know how to manage people. As a Mission Handler, you wouldn't be running in the streets; you would be the boss sitting at Headquarters, commanding the agents, and making life-or-death decisions.
Mission_Handler.day_in_the_life: You are at RAW Headquarters in Delhi. You look at global satellite maps, analyze threat reports from field agents, and brief the Prime Minister on national security. You decide when an agent goes in, and when it's time to pull them out.
Mission_Handler.alternative_match_text: If not in Intelligence, you would be a powerful IPS Officer, Corporate Strategist, or Diplomat (IFS).
Mission_Handler.roadmap: Take any stream in 11th/12th. Pursue a BA/BBA/BSc (Political Science, International Relations, or Law are great choices). The most direct route to becoming a top intelligence director in India is to crack the UPSC Civil Services Exam, become an IPS (Indian Police Service) officer, and then go on deputation to RAW or IB.
